easy.def: To do something again and again to get better.
examples: I practice piano.
She practiced her speech.
We practice every day.

more.def: To do something over and over to get better at it.
examples: I practice the piano for twenty minutes each day.
The team practices after school.
She practiced her speech in front of the mirror.

easy.def: Doing something again and again.
examples: Soccer practice is at four.
Practice helps me read.
We have band practice.

more.def: Doing something again and again to get better.
examples: Soccer practice starts at four.
It takes lots of practice to learn to juggle.
She does piano practice before dinner.

easy.def: To talk to God.
examples: We pray before dinner.
She prayed for her grandmother.
People pray in church.

more.def: To speak to God or a holy being, to give thanks or ask for help.
examples: Many families pray together before meals.
She prayed for good weather on the day of the picnic.
People gather to pray in churches, mosques and temples.

easy.def: An animal that hunts other animals for food.
examples: A lion is a predator.
A shark is a predator.
The mouse hid from the predator.

more.def: An animal that hunts and eats other animals.
examples: Owls are predators that hunt mice at night.
Wolves are predators that hunt in packs.
Without predators, there would be too many deer.

easy.def: To say what you think will happen.
examples: I predict it will rain today.
Can you predict the end of the story?
I predict we will win.

more.def: To say what you think will happen in the future, using what you already know.
examples: Scientists use clouds and wind to predict the weather.
No one can predict exactly when an earthquake will happen.
The teacher asked us to predict what would float.

easy.def: To like one thing better.
examples: I prefer pizza.
She prefers tea.
He prefers cats.

more.def: To like one thing better than another.
examples: I prefer pizza to pasta.
She prefers reading to watching TV.
Many people prefer summer to winter.

easy.def: Having a baby growing inside the body.
examples: My aunt is pregnant.
The pregnant cat sleeps a lot.
A pregnant woman rested.

more.def: Having a baby or young animal growing inside the body.
examples: My aunt is pregnant and will have a baby in May.
The pregnant cat found a quiet place to rest.
A pregnant whale swims slowly.

easy.def: To get ready.
examples: We prepare for bed by brushing our teeth.
Dad prepares lunch.
We prepare for the trip.

more.def: To get ready for something, or to make something ready.
examples: The class prepared for the play by practicing every day.
The chef prepared a special meal.
The town prepared for the storm by stacking sandbags.

easy.def: A gift.
examples: I got a present.
She wrapped the present.
The present was a book.

more.def: Something you give to someone to show love or thanks, usually on a special day.
examples: I wrapped a present for my sister's birthday.
He opened the present and found a toy train.
The best present was a visit from Grandma.

easy.def: Here, and not away.
examples: Everyone is present.
Is Sam present today?
All the kids were present.

more.def: Being in a place at a certain time.
examples: Every student was present on the day of the field trip.
Are all of the players present?
The teacher marked who was present.

easy.def: The time that is now.
examples: For the present, we will stay inside.
Do not worry about tomorrow; think about the present.
The present is the time we live in.

more.def: The time that is happening now.
examples: At present, the museum is closed for repairs.
He lives in the present and does not worry about tomorrow.
Past, present and future are the three parts of time.

easy.def: To give something to someone.
examples: She will present the prize.
I present my report.
The class presents a play.

more.def: To give or show something to a group of people.
examples: The mayor will present the award to the winner.
Our class will present a play for the school.
She presented her science project to the judges.

easy.def: The leader of some countries.
examples: The president gave a speech.
We pick a new president.
She wants to be president.

more.def: The elected leader of a country that has no king or queen.
examples: The president gave a speech to the whole nation.
Every four years, voters choose a new president.
The president met leaders from other countries.

easy.def: The person in charge of a club.
examples: Our class picked a president.
The president ran the meeting.
He is president of the chess club.

more.def: The person in charge of a club, a business or a school group.
examples: The president of the science club planned the field trip.
She was chosen president of the student council.
The president of the bank greeted the customers.

easy.def: To push on something.
examples: Press the button.
She pressed the key.
Press hard.

more.def: To push firmly on something.
examples: Press the button to start the machine.
She pressed the flower between the pages.
Press down on the lid.

easy.def: People who write and report the news.
examples: The press waited outside.
The press took pictures.
The mayor spoke to the press.

more.def: Newspapers, magazines, television and radio, and the people who report the news.
examples: The mayor answered questions from the press.
The press covered the parade.
Reporters from the press waited outside.

easy.def: A steady push against something.
examples: The pressure of the deep water pushed on the diver.
Check the tire pressure.
Press on the cut with pressure.

more.def: The force of something pressing on a surface.
examples: The pressure of the deep water squeezed the toy submarine.
Check the air pressure in the bike tires.
Press the bandage with gentle pressure.

easy.def: A worried feeling when you must do well.
examples: She felt pressure to win.
Test day brought pressure.
He handled the pressure well.

more.def: A strong feeling of worry that you must do well or do something.
examples: The final game put pressure on the players.
She felt pressure to finish the project on time.
He stayed calm under pressure.

easy.def: To act as if something is real when it is not.
examples: Let us pretend we are pirates.
I pretend to be a dog.
She pretended to sleep.

more.def: To act as if something is true when it is not, often as a game.
examples: The children pretend that the couch is a ship.
He pretended to be asleep.
We pretended to be explorers on the moon.

easy.def: Nice to look at.
examples: The flower is pretty.
She has a pretty dress.
What a pretty song!

more.def: Pleasing to look at or listen to, in a gentle way.
examples: The garden was pretty, with pink and yellow flowers.
She drew a pretty picture of the sunset.
The bird sang a pretty tune from the branch.

easy.def: A bit, but not a lot.
examples: It is pretty cold.
I am pretty tired.
The test was pretty easy.

more.def: To a fairly large degree, but not completely.
examples: The pond is pretty deep, so we stayed near the edge.
I was pretty sure that I had locked the door.
It is a pretty long walk to the library.

easy.def: How much money something costs.
examples: What is the price?
The price is low.
The price of milk went up.

more.def: The amount of money you must pay for something.
examples: The price of the toy is five dollars.
Prices are low at the farmers' market.
Check the price before you buy.

easy.def: A religious leader in some religions.
examples: The priest led the service.
A priest wore robes.
The priest blessed them.

more.def: A person who leads religious services in some religions.
examples: The priest led the service at the church.
The priest blessed the new building.
The priest visited the sick.

easy.def: The son of a king or queen.
examples: The prince wore a crown.
The prince lives in the castle.
The prince rode a horse.

more.def: The son of a king or queen, who may become king one day.
examples: The prince lived in a tall castle.
In the story, the prince searched for a lost girl.
The prince will become king one day.

easy.def: The daughter of a king or queen.
examples: The princess wore a crown.
The princess lives in a castle.
The princess rode a horse.

more.def: The daughter of a king or queen, or the wife of a prince.
examples: The princess lived in a tall castle.
In the story, the princess saves the village.
The little girl dressed as a princess.

easy.def: To put words or pictures on paper.
examples: Print the page.
She printed her name.
The machine prints pictures.

more.def: To put words or pictures on paper with a machine, or to write in separate letters.
examples: Please print your name at the top.
I printed the photo.
The machine prints a hundred pages a minute.

easy.def: A mark left by pressing.
examples: Footprints are prints.
The dog left a paw print.
We saw prints in the snow.

more.def: A mark made by pressing something onto a surface.
examples: The dog left a muddy paw print on the floor.
She saw bear prints in the snow.
The detective found a fingerprint.

easy.def: A place where people who did crimes must stay.
examples: The thief was in prison.
Prison has strong walls.
He was sent to prison.

more.def: A building where people are kept as punishment for serious crimes.
examples: The robber was sent to prison.
The old prison is now a museum.
A prison has high walls and locked doors.

easy.def: A person kept in prison.
examples: The prisoner sat in a cell.
The prisoner was in jail.
A prisoner was freed.

more.def: A person who is kept in prison or locked up.
examples: The prisoner was kept in a small cell.
In the story, the prisoner escaped.
The king freed the prisoner.

easy.def: Just for you.
examples: This is my private room.
I keep a private diary.
It is a private talk.

more.def: Belonging to one person or group and not open to everyone.
examples: This is a private beach for hotel guests only.
She wrote in her private diary.
He asked for a private talk with the teacher.

easy.def: Something hard that you must fix.
examples: We have a problem.
The problem is the door.
She fixed the problem.

more.def: Something that is hard to deal with and needs to be solved.
examples: The flat tire was a problem, so we called for help.
Our team worked together to solve the problem.
Litter on the beach is a problem for sea animals.

easy.def: A question to work out in math.
examples: I did the math problem.
This problem is hard.
Solve the problem.

more.def: A question or puzzle that you work out, especially in math.
examples: The teacher wrote a math problem on the board.
I solved the problem by drawing a picture.
Try the next problem on the page.

easy.def: A set of steps that happen in order.
examples: The process is simple.
The process of baking bread.
A growing process.

more.def: A series of steps or actions that lead to a result.
examples: The process of making bread takes several steps.
Growing a plant is a slow process.
The process of melting ice is simple.

easy.def: To treat food or materials with steps.
examples: Factories process food.
The machine processes paper.
They process milk.

more.def: To prepare or change something by a series of steps.
examples: The factory processes milk into cheese.
The machine processed the paper.
Workers process the fruit before packing it.

easy.def: Doing something as a job.
examples: A professional baseball player.
A professional cook.
She is a professional.

more.def: Doing something as a job and being paid for it.
examples: He is a professional baseball player.
A professional gardener planted the trees.
She hired a professional painter.

easy.def: A teacher at a college.
examples: The professor teaches science.
My uncle is a professor.
The professor wrote a book.

more.def: A teacher at a college or university.
examples: The professor gave a talk about volcanoes.
My aunt is a professor of history.
The professors met in the library.

easy.def: A show on TV or radio.
examples: I like this program.
The program is funny.
We watched a program about whales.

more.def: A show on television or radio.
examples: She watched a program about the ocean.
The radio program plays music for kids.
A science program comes on at six.

easy.def: A plan of things to do.
examples: The school has a reading program.
There is a summer program.
The program starts at noon.

more.def: A planned set of activities or events.
examples: The school has a program to help kids read.
The program for the concert lists every song.
He joined a swimming program at the pool.

easy.def: Instructions for a computer.
examples: I wrote a program.
The program runs the game.
A computer program shows the words.

more.def: A set of instructions that tells a computer what to do.
examples: My brother wrote a program for a math game.
The program crashed when I pressed the button.
This program helps you learn to type.

easy.def: A big school job.
examples: I am doing a science project.
The class did a project.
Our art project is due.

more.def: A piece of work with a plan, often done over a period of time.
examples: I am doing a science project on plants.
Our class did a project about the ocean.
The town started a project to build a new library.

easy.def: To say you will really do something.
examples: I promise to feed the fish.
Promise you will come back.
She promised to share.

more.def: To tell someone that you will certainly do something.
examples: He promised to return the book by Friday.
The mayor promised to fix the roads.
I promise I will not tell anyone your secret.

easy.def: Something that shows a thing is true.
examples: I have proof.
Footprints are proof.
The photo is proof.

more.def: Facts or things that show that something is true.
examples: The photo is proof that I was there.
Scientists need proof before they decide.
Muddy footprints were proof that the dog came in.

easy.def: Things that belong to someone.
examples: This is my property.
The farm is private property.
Do not touch my property.

more.def: Things that belong to a person or a group.
examples: This book is school property.
The sign said it was private property.
Please keep off my property.

easy.def: A quality of something.
examples: A property of water is that it flows.
Metal has the property of conducting heat.
A property of rubber is that it stretches.

more.def: A quality that something has.
examples: One property of water is that it flows.
Metal has the property of carrying heat.
A property of glass is that it breaks easily.

easy.def: To keep safe.
examples: A helmet protects your head.
Sunscreen protects your skin.
The dog protects the house.

more.def: To keep someone or something safe from harm.
examples: The mother bird protected her eggs from the cold.
Laws protect rare animals from hunters.
A shell protects the turtle's soft body.

easy.def: Feeling good about something you did.
examples: I am proud of my painting.
Dad is proud of me.
She was proud of her tall tower.

more.def: Feeling pleased about something you or someone else has done.
examples: Her parents were proud when she finished the race.
He is proud to be on the team.
The town is proud of its long history.

easy.def: To show that something is true.
examples: Prove that you are right.
The test proved it.
The photo proves I was there.

more.def: To show by facts that something is true.
examples: Scientists proved that the Earth goes around the sun.
Can you prove that you finished your homework?
The footprints proved a deer had been there.

easy.def: To give what is needed.
examples: The school provides lunch.
Dad provides food.
The park provides shade.

more.def: To give or supply something that is needed.
examples: The school provides lunch for all the kids.
The trees provide shade on hot days.
The camp provided tents for everyone.
